spec.name: sprint35_taker_imbalance_liquid_core
spec.hypothesis: Short-horizon taker-side order flow imbalance predicts next-N-minute directional drift in liquid, tight-spread names; prior failures (sprint32/34) were cost-driven from tail-liquidity venues, not signal absence, so testing on liquid instruments should reveal whether any exploitable edge exists before cost.
spec.power_argument: 8-symbol liquid-core basket x entry_per_day_cap=3 = up to 24 entries/day; >=300 validated trades reached in ~13 trading days within the sealed test window. sprint32/34 established realistic intraday return dispersion (~34-36bps effect scale); at n=300 this gives power to detect a mean edge >=15bps at t>=2, which is the minimum edge that could survive T1 fee costs — smaller effects are not actionable regardless of significance, avoiding an exp14-style unfalsifiable criterion.
